participants: Molly Cavanaugh (Senior SDR, Navan — external, not a Primal Instinct employee)
summary: Not a sales call and not a Primal Instinct team call. A Primal Instinct rep labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' runs a personal career-networking conversation with Molly Cavanaugh, a senior SDR at the tech company Navan, recorded on the same Fathom note-taker used for prospect calls. He describes his own background — Bentley economics and finance degree, four and a half years across Morgan Stanley wealth management, SVB structuring and Terminary Securities — and states he wants to move into B2B tech sales, ideally at an AI company or at Navan itself. Molly walks him through Navan's SDR, senior SDR and associate AE pathways, ramp periods, quota structure (three SQOs plus QDMs for a fully ramped total of six meetings a month), promotion criteria (rolling three months at 115% attainment for senior SDR, nine months in seat before an associate move), office culture and interview preparation. She offers to submit a referral for him, and he says he is already scheduled to speak with two other Navan employees, Arian and Brayden. The call ends with resume and application advice.
notable: An active Primal Instinct closer is running an external job search during the working day, recorded on the company's own meeting recorder, and the recording landed in the sales-call Drive folder alongside prospect calls.

He characterises his Primal Instinct role to an outside party not as employment but as contract work: 'I've been, you know, working at independent sales contracting job... I've been getting some closing experience there' — and dates the start to 'February of earlier this year', i.e. roughly four months of closing tenure at the time of the call.

He frames the Primal Instinct closing role as a stepping stone rather than a destination: 'now I kind of want to just transition into sales, but particularly at a tech, uh, company, tech enterprise B2B sales.'

He describes his own current sales method as script-led rather than product-led: 'I genuinely just like kind of like take the script and like go on the phone and like try to have a conversation and really just like do a good discovery and drift and handle rather than if I did know the product a little more.'
The recording was disclosed to the other party — 'I have my note taker right now' — so there is no consent issue with the capture itself.

Critically for the corpus: the speaker labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' here is 27, a Bentley graduate and US-office-based, while the speaker carrying the identical label on the sales calls in this same folder is 43, Polish and living in Poland. One label covers at least two different people.
